sections.h2: Which city office handles a Farmington Hills tax bill?
sections.html:
Farmington Hills divides the work in two: the Treasury Division mails and collects the real and personal property tax, and the Assessing Division sets a value on every parcel. Both offices share a building at 31555 West Eleven Mile Road, Farmington Hills, MI 48336, and serve the public on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30. The Treasury number is 248-871-2480 and Assessing answers at 248-871-2470.

The city lies in Oakland County, and whatever the city has not collected by early March moves to the county treasurer. Once that happens the city cannot accept payment, so the address for your check changes along with the cost of lateness.

sections.h2: When are Farmington Hills property taxes due?
sections.html:
Farmington Hills uses two bills a year. The summer bill is due without penalty from July 1 to August 31, and the winter bill from December 1 to February 16. The city's property tax page sets out the full calendar.

Farmington Hills summer and winter bill calendar, from the city's tax page
ItemSummer billWinter bill
MailedJune 30November 30
Pay without penaltyJuly 1 to August 31December 1 to February 16
Penalty addedSeptember 1, at 4%February 17, at 4%
Interest1/2% a monthNone listed
Last day to pay at City HallMarch 1March 1
Goes to Oakland CountyMarch 2March 2

The page also warns that a bill that never arrived still carries the tax and any late charges. After a purchase, a move or a land contract, tell Assessing so the next bill reaches the right person.

sections.h2: How is a Farmington Hills assessment set, and how do you challenge it?
sections.html:
The city aims for an assessed value equal to half of market value. Assessing studies 24 months of sales so that similar homes land in line, and each parcel is tied to a parcel number, a legal description and an address.

The State Tax Commission recommends reviewing roughly a fifth of properties each year, so an appraiser may stop by to look at your exterior. Notices of assessment go out every February, laying out the proposed valuation, the property class, principal residence exemption status, transfer status and appeal rights.

  • Read the February notice and the record card for errors in square footage, class or exemption status.
  • Call 248-871-2470 for an informal meeting with the assessor or staff before the March Board of Review.
  • Take a written appeal or an appointment request to the Board of Review in March.
  • Ask for copies of your records by phone or in person; broader requests go through the City Clerk as a records request.

Keep the bill dates in the table above in mind while an appeal is open, since the due dates run on their own calendar.

sections.h2: How can you pay a Farmington Hills property tax bill?
sections.html:
The city recommends echecks, which post the same day with no fee. If one bounces, a $30 insufficient-funds charge follows.

  • Debit or credit card online, or by phone at 734-402-8271, for 2.8% plus 50 cents per payment.
  • In person at the Treasury counter during office hours.
  • A drive-up drop box in front of Police Headquarters, for checks only.
  • Mail to the city lockbox in Detroit, where payment counts when it is received, not when it is postmarked.

Confirm the parcel ID first, since sending money to the wrong property is the taxpayer's problem. A mailed payment needs the bill's top coupon and a check with your parcel number and phone number written on it. Do not mail after the due date.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Farmington Hills taxes?
sections.html:
Balances still open on March 2 pass to the Oakland County Treasurer. According to the city, taxes for 2025 and earlier years have already been turned over, and checks go to the Oakland County Treasurer at 1200 N Telegraph Road, Pontiac, Michigan 48341-0479. Call the county at 248-858-0611.

Before picking a closing date, get a payoff number from the county. MCL 211.135 calls for certificates from the county and city treasurers on tax liens and five years of payments before certain deeds can be recorded, which is why a title company wants any balance cleared at the table.

sections.h2: What relief exists for Farmington Hills homeowners?
sections.html:
The city publishes a deferment application for summer taxes on a principal residence. For 2026, a household with 2025 income under $40,000 could defer the summer bill until February 16, 2027 if the owner is at least 62, or is totally and permanently disabled, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic or quadriplegic, or is an eligible serviceperson, veteran, widow or widower.

The same page points owners to the Assessing Division for questions about the homestead exemption, hardship or veteran's exemptions and taxable value. The city also links a list of state property tax assistance programs.

sections.h2: What is Farmington Hills like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Farmington Hills covers 33.31 square miles in Oakland County, bordered by West Bloomfield to the north, Franklin and Southfield to the east, Livonia to the south and Novi to the west. The area began as the Quaker settlement of Quakertown after Arthur Power bought land in 1823, and Farmington Township was organized in 1827.

The economy runs on offices and engineering. Nissan's North American technical center, the United States headquarters of Bosch, Mercedes-Benz Financial Services and Beaumont Hospital, the city's largest employer in its 2019 financial report, are all in the city. Oakland Community College has its Orchard Ridge campus here.

Almost all of the city is in Farmington Public Schools, and small portions are in Clarenceville and Walled Lake Consolidated. The main roads are M-5, Orchard Lake Road, 12 Mile Road, I-696 and I-275, with SMART buses serving the area. The former Harrison High School building was reused as a community center called The Hawk.

sections.h2: What does a Farmington Hills seller owe at closing besides property tax?
sections.html:
The state transfer tax, $3.75 per $500 of value under MCL 207.525, lands on the grantor under MCL 207.523. At the QuickFacts median of $354,500 the math is 709 slices and $2,658.75, paid to the county treasurer inside 15 days of the deed being delivered.

A county transfer tax and recording fees come on top, and Oakland County's register sets its own charges. Before signing, ask the closing agent for a written statement showing the tax certificate, any open summer or winter balance and the recording costs.

sections.h2: How do Farmington Hills housing numbers look?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts, using survey years 2020 to 2024, list these figures for the city.

  • An estimated 83,291 residents as of July 2025, 0.9% fewer than the 2020 base.
  • A typical owned home is valued at $354,500, and owners occupy 64.7% of housing.
  • 35,529 households earn a median of $104,836.
  • Renters pay a median of $1,551 a month, and 57.6% of adults over 25 have a four-year degree.

These are citywide medians, and individual blocks will differ.

faqs.q: When is the winter tax bill due in Farmington Hills?
faqs.a: December 1 through February 16 without penalty. The bill is mailed November 30, and a 4% penalty is added on February 17.

faqs.q: Where do I pay old Farmington Hills taxes?
faqs.a: At the Oakland County Treasurer, not the city. Per the city's page, taxes from 2025 and earlier have been turned over to the county at 1200 N Telegraph Road in Pontiac, phone 248-858-0611.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Farmington Hills property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments add 2.8% plus $0.50. Echecks have no fee, though a returned one costs $30.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Farmington Hills assessment?
faqs.a: Call Assessing at 248-871-2470 for an informal meeting, then use the March Board of Review, either by appointment or by letter received before the last meeting day.

faqs.q: Can seniors delay Farmington Hills summer taxes?
faqs.a: Possibly. The city's deferment form for 2026 covered owners 62 or older, or disabled, blind or a qualifying veteran or surviving spouse, with 2025 household income under $40,000. Ask Treasury for the current form.
